specific_prose_corrections: Four data rows are explained before use; columns represent input and negative storage, while coefficient order and response order are explicit.
The two-row chain-rule bridge is retained and expanded; residual e_i differs from the physical rate r, and the full loss averages all four rows.
Quadratic gradients and Hessians connect to local Taylor changes, stationary counterexamples and the distinction between one-point curvature and whole-domain convexity.
One-dimensional update factors explain convergence, equal-amplitude alternation and divergence; the strict all-initial-state step range remains intact.
Newton direction and step length are checked separately. Quartic negative curvature is computed explicitly, and local quadratic convergence conditions remain beside the reasoning.
Armijo half-step equality remains accepted, and accepting one step is separated from gradient stopping or exhausted update/trial counts.
Ridge uniqueness is separated from mechanism identification; feature-coordinate shrinkage, mean-loss normalization and conditional Gaussian-prior interpretation are retained.
Absolute-value subgradients and their set notation are explained before the proximal optimality condition; a one-step target is worked through with threshold eta*lambda.
Training-only scaling, the constant-column convention, intercept and validation/test roles are connected to a hand calculation and original-coordinate prediction.
Two-input constraints specify common flow scaling, each inequality row, multiplier order and four residual meanings; the boundary optimum is calculated before KKT.
Qualification-dependent necessity and convex sufficiency remain distinct; the degenerate x^2<=0 counterexample, active-set enumeration and finite square-penalty violation are retained.
Capstone fitting coefficients and decision inputs use separate meanings and targets. MSE equals twice the restored half-square loss; numerical-failure returns no longer imply proven infeasibility.
